Test 9 uses `sends=[[4,0,2,0]]` (code 2 = link 1) but `fab` has only 1 link (codes 0,1). Per contract, trace "directed codes" are valid — my test violates that. Also "not_in_slice" is about the link not being listed in the current slice — with one link and slices=[[0]] link 0 is always in the slice... To test not_in_slice I need 2 slices: Q=2 so some phases use slice1 (empty). Let me redo test 9:

- Fabric: slices [[0],[]] (link 0 in slice 0 only), S=8, T=1, O=0 → P = Q*S/gcd(T,Q*S) = 16/gcd(1,16)=16. Phase p: slice = floor(p/8) % 2 → p in 0..7 → slice 0; p in 8..15 → slice 1. So send at tick 8 (phase 8) → not_in_slice ✓. But R must be > 8... R=10, rates 10 rows.

- blackout: fabric with blackouts [[0,0,16]] (all phases) and send at tick 0 → 'blackout'.
- guard: guard 2, rho at phase 0 = 0 → 0 < 2 → 'guard' ✓ (need blackout-free fabric).
- port_busy after guard pass ✓ tested in test 1.

Also the engine crashed with IndexError — contract says codes are valid so it's not a required behavior, but robustness is nice; leave as is (inputs are guaranteed valid).

Let me rewrite test 9.

content.text: My test used an out-of-range directed code (contract guarantees valid codes). Rewriting test 9 with a proper 2-slice fabric:

arguments.command:
cd /workspace/tmp && python3 - << 'EOF'
src = open('test_replay2.py').read()
old_start = src.index("# 9. status precedence")
old_end = src.index("# 10. peak with signed errors")
new = '''# 9. status precedence: not_in_slice > blackout > guard > port_busy
fab9a = base(slices=[[0],[]])           # link 0 only in slice 0
# P=16: phases 0..7 slice 0, 8..15 slice 1
tr = trace(rounds=10, rates_ppb=[[0,0]]*10, sends=[[4,8,0,0]], queries=[9])
res = run([{"op":"replay","profile":prof,"fabric":fab9a,"guard_ns":0,"trace":tr}])[0]
assert res['send_status']==['not_in_slice'], res
fab9b = base(blackouts=[[0,0,16]])
tr = trace(rounds=2, rates_ppb=[[0,0],[0,0]], sends=[[4,0,0,0]])
res = run([{"op":"replay","profile":prof,"fabric":fab9b,"guard_ns":0,"trace":tr}])[0]
assert res['send_status']==['blackout'], res
# blackout covering only the arrival interval is allowed (boundary-aligned arrival)
fab9c = base(blackouts=[[0,1,2]])       # blackout only phase 1
# delay 1, T=1 -> arrival at boundary 1 exactly; flight covers interval 0 only
tr = trace(rounds=3, rates_ppb=[[0,0]]*3, sends=[[4,0,0,0]], queries=[1])
res = run([{"op":"replay","profile":prof,"fabric":fab9c,"guard_ns":0,"trace":tr}])[0]
assert res['send_status']==['sent'], res
# delay 2 crosses interval 1 -> blackout
fab9d = base(blackouts=[[0,1,2]],
             links=[{"ends":[[0,0,0],[1,0,0]],"delay_ns":[2,2],"defer_rounds":[0,0]}])
tr = trace(rounds=3, rates_ppb=[[0,0]]*3, sends=[[4,0,0,0]], queries=[1])
res = run([{"op":"replay","profile":prof,"fabric":fab9d,"guard_ns":0,"trace":tr}])[0]
assert res['send_status']==['blackout'], res
tr = trace(rounds=2, rates_ppb=[[0,0],[0,0]], sends=[[4,0,0,0]])
res = run([{"op":"replay","profile":prof,"fabric":base(),"guard_ns":2,"trace":tr}])[0]
assert res['send_status']==['guard'], res   # rho=0 < 2
print('status precedence ok')

'''
src = src[:old_start] + new + src[old_end:]
open('test_replay2.py','w').write(src)
EOF
cd /workspace/tmp && python3 test_replay2.py
